name: as-forage-and-survival
title: Forage Both & Outlive a Non-Mover
question: Does the evolved forager keep both nutrients alive by visiting both resources, and does it survive longer than a passive agent?
claim: The agent forages both resources in 12 of 16 FAR, high-drain environments (sep 42-62, asymmetric per-nutrient drain) and is STATE-DEPENDENT: it uses its internal nutrient sensors to prioritize the faster-draining resource (ablating them costs +226 survival + 2 forages-both), rather than the blind circling of the earlier regime.

expected_behavior.name: forages-both-and-outlives-nonmover
expected_behavior.condition: committed M2 seed, 16 FAR high-drain environments (sep 42-62, asymmetric drain), max_steps 2000
expected_behavior.rationale: Forages both resources in >=11/16 (achieved 12/16); AND genuinely uses internal state — ablating the nutrient sensors measurably hurts foraging (state-dependent switching, not blind circling). Verified in tests/test_forager_seed.py.

findings.summary: Forages both in 12/16 far high-drain environments (survival ~2098); STATE-DEPENDENT — prioritizes the fast-draining resource, ablation of the nutrient sensors costs +226 survival + 2 forages-both (was 0 for the old blind circler).
findings.detail: figures/forage.gif shows the agent shuttling between resources while both nutrient bars are sustained; figures/trajectory_nutrients.png shows the spatial loop + nutrient time series.
